rows.en: All I could do was remember.

ghs.en: Even only to remember.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says all the narrator can do is remember them. The English is an incomplete subordinate phrase and omits the limiting predicate.
ghs.remedy: All I can do is remember them.

ghs.en: Indescribably so.

rows.jp: 祠によりかかって、目を閉じた。
rows.en: I leaned against the shrine and closed my eyes.

ghs.en: I leaned onto the hokora and closed my eyes.

rows.jp: 名状しがたい、奇妙な眩暈感に包まれる。
rows.en: An indescribably strange vertigo enveloped me.

ghs.en: I am engulfed by a strange vertigo, difficult to describe.

rows.jp: ゆらゆらと世界が揺れている気がして、三半規管が錯覚を起こした。
rows.en: The world seemed to sway, fooling my inner ear.

ghs.en: The world felt like it was slowly swaying from one side to the other, semicircular canals causing illusions.

rows.jp: ずっと二人のことばかり、考え続けていた。
rows.en: I had spent all that time thinking of nothing but the two of them.

ghs.en: And all along I did nothing but continue thinking about those two.
Consciousness grows dim,

rows.jp: 重く機能を停止する身体。
rows.en: My body ground heavily to a halt.

ghs.en: the body suspends primary functions.

rows.jp: 一切が分解されて構成される過程を、ヒトの知覚力は観測することができない。
rows.en: Human perception could not observe the process by which everything was decomposed and composed anew.

ghs.en: The process of complete dismantlement and reconstruction is something that cannot be observed by the powers of perception of a mere person.

rows.jp: たやすく分解される世界。

ghs.en: The world can be dismantled so easily...

rows.jp: いつ終わるとも知れない。
rows.en: There was no knowing when it would end.

ghs.en: When it will end I can never know.

rows.jp: そんな場所で、俺は、生きていく。
rows.en: In such a place, I would go on living.

ghs.en: And this is the place in which I go to live.
The struggle continues.
